script_lines.text: The Empathia website’s demo link opens here. Everything in this demonstration is invented and runs in your browser: synthetic data, simulated adapters, and nothing connected to a real building.
North Campus: three buildings and thirty rooms, generated from one seeded dataset. One room is complete, three keep earlier records, and the other twenty-six are outlines, with no invented detail.
Atlas Tower has twelve floors. Only the floors that hold rooms of the campus model open; a floor with nothing recorded says so.
Floor four holds three rooms of the model on a schematic floor plate. Atlas 4.218, the boardroom, is the reference room, drawn in full.

Camera 1, at position A-0106. The unit there now is AS-0112, a Logitech Rally Camera named from its published specification page; anything not read from that page says ‘spec to verify’. The panel shows its baseline entry, its drift and the tests that cover it.

Search Party answers from the records: the AV Operations team for Atlas Tower, the integrator and its agreement, and who to escalate to. Every relationship says how it is known; the support model is declared, not guessed.

Core Replay plays this room’s history from the synthetic event log, one recorded event at a time; there is no video. Months after acceptance, a change to replace the front camera like for like is approved by someone other than the person who asked for it.

The commissioning engine reopened twelve tests; each was re-run on the new unit and verified by a second person. Re-acceptance is still held on one design finding, its exception pending. The button here is a labelled scenario action that changes only this browser’s demo workspace.
Room Story assembles the same records from request to lesson: revisions, approvals, tests, baselines and repairs, with who did each and how it is evidenced. Where nothing is recorded, it says so.
Start from a room that is already installed. Field Intelligence can take it on as an existing installation, and this link replays that onboarding scan on the room’s own views.

Observe Only reads the records, a synthetic discovery fixture and published specifications. It moves nothing, plays no sound and changes no configuration; passive network checks are not run in a browser.

Supervised Commissioning waits for a technician before any physical step. The replay stops at its first approval: a bounded camera sweep of A-0106 and A-0107. Every physical action here is a simulation, and no hardware command is sent.
With each step approved, the scan report sorts twenty-one findings into known, inferred and requires verification. Not one is measured, because no instrument is connected.
The commissioning engine derives seventy-five tests for this design, each with the reason it applies. The results are a synthetic seed, each recorded by one person and verified by another.

When the front camera was replaced, the engine read the change from the installation records and reopened twelve of the seventy-five tests. Their earlier results stay on record, but they no longer count.
The evidence ledger lists the room’s canonical event log: who did what, when, and to which record. Anything you do in this browser is listed separately, kept apart from the seeded record.

The Assurance engine compares the room with its accepted baseline. After a re-tune, the audio processor’s configuration signature on record no longer matches baseline v1. Fourteen dimensions are not assessed, because nothing was measured.
For the audio dropout that came back, APEX ranks hypotheses and says why none is proven. It is labelled modeled: no diagnosis has been opened on record.
Search Party then looks across all five incidents on record for what they share. Three rooms on one access switch have raised incidents: a lead to follow, not a conclusion.
SIGNAL lesson A12 is about speech intelligibility in a meeting room. The scenario quotes the lesson, then asks you to fix the room, decide, and check your fix on a take you have not heard.
The Audio Lab is a working Web Audio channel strip on synthesized voices. Change the EQ or the gain, and the sound and its spectrum change with it. Sound plays only when you press Play.
The challenge: make the conference-room voice intelligible. The score is an educational approximation computed from the processed signal, not a speech transmission measurement.
The Camera Lab renders a conference room. Exposure, white balance and framing change the picture, and its readouts are computed from the pixels of that rendered frame.
The Lighting Lab has five fixtures, a DMX patch with overlap checks, and cues with fades. The DMX output is simulated and kept flash-safe.
A saved lab attempt becomes a synthetic training record in this browser. It can support an internal competency assessment as evidence; it is never a credential and never counts for dispatch.

And back to the room the lesson came from: the audio processor of Atlas 4.218, where incident ISS-0417 is open. Its device panel links straight to the Audio Lab, so practice and the room’s record stay one step apart.
